question: What is the value of \(a\) for which \[\dfrac{1}{\log_2 a} + \dfrac{1}{\log_3 a} + \dfrac{1}{\log_4 a} = 1?\]
solution:
The original logarithms require \(a>0\), and their denominators are nonzero exactly when \(a\ne1\). On this domain, change of base gives
\[
\frac{1}{\log_b a}=\log_a b.
\]
This makes all three terms logarithms with the same base, allowing us to combine them:
\[
\log_a2+\log_a3+\log_a4
=\log_a(2\cdot3\cdot4)
=\log_a24.
\]
The given equation is therefore \(\log_a24=1\). By the definition of a logarithm, this means \(a^1=24\), so \(a=24\). This value satisfies \(a>0\) and \(a\ne1\), and every transformation was reversible on that domain. Hence the answer is \(\boxed{24}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
